calls.head: Who drives the play: the Hurricanes
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Flyers near the bottom. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Flyers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 31% chance, and it went the way we feared.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 69% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Philadelphia’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Philadelphia has had one of the league’s least effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Philadelphia’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.5 (about 6.8 against Carolina) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 7.0% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 62 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.
surprises.flipped: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams

story.head: Still no win for the Flyers
paras: It was a busy second period. Andrei Svechnikov and Shayne Gostisbehere scored three and a half minutes apart midway through the period to put the Hurricanes up 2-0. Christian Dvorak got the Flyers on the board less than two minutes later, but that was as close as they got. Sebastian Aho made it 3-1 for the Hurricanes a minute and a half later. Mark Jankowski stretched the lead to 4-1 with just under five minutes left, his fourth straight game with a goal.

The Hurricanes drove the play, outshooting the Flyers 30-19, and the scoreboard caught up. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves for the Hurricanes, and Joseph Woll stopped 26 of 30 at the other end. The Canes moved to 5-1-1, climbing into first in the NHL in points. The Flyers are still last in the Metropolitan. The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-5-2.

items.text: The Hurricanes are rolling: five straight wins.
Sebastian Aho has a point in six straight games.
Jackson Blake’s five-game point streak ended.
